reason: The cited lines show a handler sending a fixed socket message to go forward, and optionally returning the current page URL, title, and browser/ARIA snapshot. They do not show arbitrary host code execution. They do not deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination. The returned page URL/title/snapshot can contain web page content controlled by the page/site, so UNTRUSTED is supported. Although browser page contents might include private data in some contexts, these lines alone do not establish that non-public data such as host files, intranet, or credentialed SaaS data is accessed or returned, so SECRET is insufficient.
